suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-28 adds this relationship only as a bounded systemic-sclerosis lung-involvement association. Systemic sclerosis is frequently accompanied by interstitial lung disease, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish ILD in every person or determine an individual's cause, severity, or course. Require independently documented systemic sclerosis and ILD, compatible pulmonary phenotype and chronology, objective testing, and pulmonology/rheumatology review. Preserve smoking, occupational exposure, infection, hypersensitivity, medication toxicity, idiopathic ILD, and other competing causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of systemic sclerosis and interstitial lung disease with a defined radiographic or physiologic phenotype
Pulmonary-function testing, high-resolution CT, oxygenation, and longitudinal severity records
Chronology of systemic-sclerosis activity, ILD onset, progression, and treatment

Pulmonology or rheumatology assessment distinguishing systemic-sclerosis-associated ILD from other etiologies

sourceReferences.citation: Perelas A, Silver RM, Arrossi AV, Highland KB. Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease. Lancet Respir Med. 2020;8(3):304-320. PMID 32113575. doi:10.1016/S2213-2600(19)30480-1.
sourceReferences.note: Review of systemic-sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Systemic sclerosis is clinically associated with interstitial lung disease, but population or review evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without diagnosis, phenotype, chronology, objective pulmonary findings, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Systemic sclerosis can involve the lungs through disease-related immune and fibrotic processes, but the precise contribution and individual clinical pathway must be established from the patient's phenotype and objective longitudinal pulmonary evidence.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease is a recognized clinical pattern, but the review does not establish that systemic sclerosis caused or aggravated ILD in every individual; diagnosis, phenotype, chronology, objective testing, treatment, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent systemic-sclerosis and ILD diagnoses; defined radiographic and physiologic phenotype; chronology and longitudinal pulmonary testing; exposure, infection, hypersensitivity, medication, and idiopathic alternatives; specialist assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Smoking, occupational, environmental, or biomass exposure
Medication toxicity, infection, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, or another connective-tissue disease
Idiopathic or unrelated interstitial lung disease
